posts.name: Sumedhik Bandyopadhyay
posts.cooked:
If I don’t remember where exactly within the output of the ‘uname -a’ command, the architecture of the system is present, how should one go about this. Although simply using uname -p provides the architecture directly, what about in case when the options don’t immediately come to mind?

Thank You

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
You are not supposed to memorize the location. You can simply run uname -a, see the column in which it is present, then use cut to get that column. You do not get a single chance to solve a programming style question.

Yes, uname -p gives the answer directly as well.

posts.name: Sumedhik Bandyopadhyay
posts.cooked: Right, I forgot that the OPPE will be taking place within VM and not onto the GPA - PPA interface of the dashboard, thank you

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Even in the dashboard interface, you are allowed multiple submissions, and can purposefully write incomplete commands to see the full output first and then write the cut by counting the columns.
